The '''risk inclination formula''' uses the principle of moments, or [[Varignon's theorem (mechanics)|Varignon's theorem]],<ref>
{{cite book
|last=Coxeter
|first=H. S. M. |author-link=H. S. M. Coxeter
|title=Quadrangles: Varignon's Theorem. Geometry Revisited
|year=1967
|publisher=The Mathematical Association of America
|location=Washington, D.C.
|pages=51–55
}}
</ref><ref>
{{cite book
|last=Sharma
|first=D. P.
|title=Engineering Mechanics
|year=2010
|publisher=IDK Kindersley
|location=New Delhi, India
|pages=8–9
}}
</ref> to calculate the first [[factorial moment]] of [[probability]] in order to define this center point of balance among all [[confidence weighting|confidence weights]] (i.e., the point of risk equilibration).

The formal derivation of the RIF is divided into three separate calculations: (1) calculation of 1st factorial moment, (2) calculation of inclination, and (3) calculation of the risk inclination score.

The RIF <ref>{{cite conference |url=http://www.eric.ed.gov/ERICWebPortal/search/recordDetails.jsp?searchtype=basic&pageSize=10&ERICExtSearch_Facet_0=facet_au&ERICExtSearch_SearchValue_0=Brady+Michael+Jack&ERICExtSearch_FacetValue_0=%22Jack%2C+Brady%22&ERICExtSearch_SearchType_0=au&_pageLabel=RecordDetails&objectId=0900019b8046c889&accno=ED519174&_nfls=false |title=Utilitarian Model of Confidence Testing for Knowledge-based Societies |last1=Jack |first1=B.M. |last2=Hung |first2=K.M.|last3=Liu |first3=C.J.|last4=Chiu |first4=H.L.|publisher=ERIC |id= ED519174}},</ref> is a component of the [[risk inclination model]].
